summary.headline: FY26 PAT rose 70% to INR 72 crore, a company record, but Q4 loss before tax widened to INR 16.4 crore on low wind.
summary.overview: FY26 total income and EBITDA were about INR 316 crore and INR 206 crore, up 13% and 10% YoY, helped by favourable first-half wind, a refund of excess interest from earlier periods, and a about 21% fall in interest cost. Q4 FY26 was weaker: total income and EBITDA were marginally lower at about INR 46 crore and INR 18 crore, and loss before exceptional items and tax was about INR 16.4 crore versus INR 14.7 crore a year earlier, due to low wind availability. Operating capacity is about 399 MW (392 MW wind, 7 MW solar), with 9.9 MW of wind added in FY26 and 17.6 MW of solar under construction. Management said the 1 GW target is still on, but external equity needed for larger deals has slowed given market conditions, and no timeline was given.

financial_highlights.change: Lower debt and 45 bps cut in rate on largest loan

financial_highlights.metric: Loss before exceptional items and tax Q4 FY26
financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR 14.7 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Wind
segments.commentary: 392 MW operating wind capacity; 9.9 MW added in FY26 (6.6 MW end-March 2026, 3.3 MW April 2026). Q4 wind availability was lower than last year, with the company citing low wind across the industry. 7.8 MW of older turbines has entered repowering under the Tamil Nadu policy.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: 7 MW solar plant commissioned in December 2025. A further 17.6 MW is under construction, expected to be commissioned in Q1 FY27 and reach full production during Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Croatia wind
segments.commentary: 10.5 MW wind asset in Croatia, mentioned in the company overview; no separate financials discussed.

guidance_outlook: Upcoming wind season starts by end-May 2026; the 9.9 MW added recently will be fully available for it.
17.6 MW solar: about INR 14.5 crore revenue and INR 12.8 crore EBITDA on a full-year basis, lower in FY27 because of part-year operation.
9.9 MW wind: about INR 14 crore revenue and INR 10 crore EBITDA in a normal wind year.
Management said the 1 GW renewable target remains on, but gave no timeline; an announcement on external equity was guided to possibly come in the next quarter.
Further repowering additions are possible during FY27; capacity plans beyond this year are still a work in progress.
capex_capacity: Operating capacity about 399 MW as of FY26 end: 392 MW wind and 7 MW solar.
9.9 MW wind added in FY26 (6.6 MW end-March 2026, 3.3 MW April 2026).
17.6 MW solar under construction, commissioning in Q1 FY27.
Repowering of 7.8 MW older wind turbines started under the Tamil Nadu repowering policy; other older assets are being reviewed.
New capacity takes six to eight months to build; this year's planned additions are already covered.
Battery storage added to solar is under evaluation to meet 24x7 customer demand.
demand_pricing: Tariffs were fixed through the year, as most capacity is C&I or under long-term PPAs; no material evacuation issues were reported.
Receivables exposure is limited to Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat state electricity boards; management sees no significant payment stickiness.
No curtailment issues currently; only technical curtailment from breakdowns in recent years.
Solar grid glut in afternoon hours; company will be more cautious on solar expansion and keep expanding wind.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 1 GW target be funded, and is there a timeline? Will the company do a preferential issue or rights issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all options are being considered and strategic acquisitions have slowed due to market volatility. No timeline was given beyond a possible update in the next quarter. Control retention was described as a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company reach 1 GW without buying assets, and will EBITDA go to debt repayment or dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus cash flow goes to early loan repayment under loan terms, mainly at the Beta subsidiary. Management said small expansions of about 50 MW are possible with internal resources, but larger growth needs external equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 FY26 revenue fall despite strong full-year growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 is normally a low-wind quarter and wind was even lower this year. Management said this was industry-wide and not specific to the company.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and EBITDA will the 17.6 MW solar and 9.9 MW wind add in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar: about INR 14.5 crore revenue and INR 12.8 crore EBITDA on a full-year basis. Wind: about INR 14 crore revenue and INR 10 crore EBITDA in a normal wind year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove higher Q4 depreciation and other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation rose by about INR 1 crore from new capitalisation; new assets carry no O&M cost in year one. Other expenses rose on legal and consultancy charges and a one-time write-off of about INR 1.67 crore of long-overdue balances.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q1 FY27 profit recover, and which segment will drive growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarters should be compared year-on-year, not sequentially, since wind varies by quarter. Wind remains the main growth driver; solar expansion will be cautious and battery storage is being evaluated.

risks_watch: Wind variability: Q4 showed the sharp impact of low wind on a quarter with a loss before tax.
Funding of the 1 GW target: no timeline and external equity still pending; promoter control is a stated constraint.
Shareholder returns: surplus cash is directed to early loan repayment, so no dividend was indicated.
Ramp-up of 17.6 MW solar in Q1-Q2 FY27 and the 9.9 MW wind in the upcoming season.
Repowering economics and the scope of further repowering are still open.
Receivables from AP and Gujarat state electricity boards.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and the FY26 record profit, but guarded on strategy: management declined to give timelines or values for acquisitions and equity raising, citing market volatility and listing rules. Evasive on the 1 GW target funding and valuation questions, repeatedly deferring to future updates.
key_quotes: FY26 was a breakthrough year for the company with many 'Firsts'.
But this variation will be there. In the renewable energy business, this kind of variation quarter-on-quarter, year-on-year will always be there because we have to take the wind comes.
We are, in fact, looking at whether it makes sense for us to add battery storage to the solar capacity in order to make it more customer-friendly because our customers need 24x7 power.
We cannot talk about all this until it happens. We are a listed company.
